question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+y,\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\text{E}[Y]=\frac{7}{12},$ and $E[{X}^{2}]=\frac{5}{12},$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $Σ$ is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2},
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

First, we find $\text{Var}[X].$ Using the given results, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}-{(\frac{7}{12})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{144}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we compute $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}(x+y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x{y}^{2}+{y}^{3})\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+x{y}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}+{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{6}{y}^{3}+\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}-{(\frac{7}{12})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{144}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's find $\text{Cov}[X,Y].$ By the rule of the lazy statistician, we find $\text{E}[XY]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}xy(x+y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2})\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}y+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{3}y+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{6}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-(\frac{7}{12})\cdot (\frac{7}{12}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{144}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{11}{144} & -\frac{1}{144} \\ -\frac{1}{144} & \frac{11}{144}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{144}[\begin{aligned}11 & -1 \\ -1 & 11\end{aligned}].
$$
